newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas criticises U.S. for not freeing Abu Marzook.
newsitem.headline: Hamas criticises U.S. for not freeing Abu Marzook.

text.p: Hamas demanded on Wednesday the United States speed up the release of Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook, a political leader of the militant Moslem group, now that Israel has dropped an extradition request.

"The information coming to us indicate that the American authorities are trying to evade the inevitable release of Dr Mousa Abu Marzook by refusing to close the file of extradition to the Zionist enemy," Hamas's politbureau said in a statement faxed to an international news agency.
"We in the Islamic Resistance Movement (Hamas) demand the U.S. administration stop procrastinating and not resort to any evasive measures that would extend (his) detention," it said.

Israel withdrew its request for extradition of Abu Marzook, 46, who has been imprisoned in New York for the last 21 months. Israeli security sources said Israel feared Abu Marzook's imprisonment in the Jewish state would draw Hamas reprisals.

U.S. authorities are now pursuing earlier efforts to have him "excluded" from the United States under a 1990 law that refuses admission to aliens engaged in or giving material support to "terrorist" activities.
A prosecutor told a U.S. federal judge on Monday that Abu Marzook must either contest or concede that he was involved in "terrorist" activities before he can be deported.
Under the law, Abu Marzook could be sent to the country of his birth, the country of his nationality, the country he had most recently left or another that might accept him.
Abu Marzook told Reuters in an interview last week that he believed a deal had been struck in which he would be deported to Jordan.
Hamas said that U.S. attempts to prolong Abu Marzook's detention "demonstrates the falsity of American justice whenever the issue pertained to Islam and its supporters".

The group said it held "the U.S. administration and the Zionist enemy -- who we see as the direct reason for the suffering of brother and holy struggler Dr Abu Marzook -- fully resopnsible for his continued incarceration".
But the statement stopped short of making any threats against the United States.
